chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife. He said: 'He inherits her and she inherits him as long as the revocable divorce (raj'ah) remains for him over her.' The discussion regarding this report is the same as the discussion regarding the first report. As for the two reports that we presented earlier, one from Ubayd ibn Zurara and the other from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from his saying: 'When he divorces her for the third time, she inherits him,' these do not indicate that he does not inherit her except through the implication of the context (dalil al-khitab), which may be set aside for a stronger evidence. And we have already presented what indicates that from it, namely the hadith of Abd al-Rahman from Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), when he asked him about a man who divorced his wife with her final divorce, he said: 'They inherit each other during the waiting period (iddah).' And this is explicit regarding what we said.

key_terms.العِدّة: Waiting period (iddah) after divorce or death
key_terms.دَلِيلُ الخِطَاب: Implication of the context (a principle in interpreting texts where meaning is suggested but not explicitly stated)
key_terms.رَجعَةٌ: Revocable divorce (the husband can take back his wife without a new contract during the iddah)

ai.seo_question: Do a husband and wife inherit each other during the waiting period of a revocable divorce?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi synthesizes conflicting reports by distinguishing between the explicit textual implication (dalil al-khitab) and definitive proof, ultimately affirming that spouses inherit each other during the iddah of a final divorce (talaq mughallazah) based on the clear narration of Abd al-Rahman from Musa al-Kadhim. This resolution underscores the Shia juristic principle that the marital bond persists for inheritance purposes until the completion of the waiting period, regardless of whether the divorce is revocable or irrevocable.
